topics.title: Deterministic Policy Engines (OPAL & OPA / Rego)
questions: Why use OPAL or OPA instead of hardcoding authorization in your application or API gateway?
How do you handle low-latency policy evaluation in distributed microservices?
Explain how Policy-as-Code scales across Kubernetes clusters.
topics.opening_hook: In high-consequence distributed architectures, authorization logic evolves at a fundamentally different velocity than business logic, making in-code checks an audit liability.
architecture_points: Decouples authorization completely: Policy is authored as declarative Rego v1, version-controlled in Git, and synced real-time via OPAL WebSockets.
Zero network hops on critical path: OPA runs as an in-memory local sidecar (localhost:8181) or embedded Go library inside the service mesh.
Cryptographically verifiable audit trails: Every evaluation decision produces an immutable bundle log shipped to telemetry without impacting request throughput.
Real-time state hydration: OPAL monitors Kafka/Postgres CDC triggers and pushes state deltas to OPA sidecars in under 50ms.
metrics: 19.9 µs/op evaluation latency in Rego benchmark
> 50,000 policy evaluations per second per core
Zero downtime policy updates without microservice pod restarts
topics.tradeoffs: Sidecar memory overhead vs centralized latency; local cache freshness vs instant revocation guarantees.
topics.counter_question: How is your team currently handling dynamic permission invalidation across your distributed edge nodes when user roles change?

topics.title: Autonomous UAV Swarms & Edge Robotics
questions: How do you handle consensus and mission synchronization when UAVs face packet loss or radio silence?
What architecture guarantees fail-safe operation in multi-agent autonomous robotics?
How do you avoid single points of failure in swarm coordination?
topics.opening_hook: We design for partition tolerance from day one using leaderless decentralized state machines rather than fragile centralized ground stations.
architecture_points: Decentralized state vector: Each UAV continuously tracks battery reserve, sensor coverage cone, and Euclidean distance to mission waypoints.
Gossip over MAVLink/ROS2 DDS: Asynchronous peer-to-peer sync allows the swarm to maintain collective situational awareness under high packet loss.
Deterministic fallback routines: If RF communication drops below threshold, nodes execute localized geometric containment or return-to-rendezvous routines.
Cost-utility task allocation: Dynamic Hungarian algorithm optimizes workload assignment weighted against individual battery degradation curves.
metrics: < 15ms local consensus convergence over ad-hoc mesh
100% mission preservation during up to 40% node loss
Deterministic fail-safe transition under 250ms of RF loss
topics.tradeoffs: Local battery compute budget vs cryptographic signature overhead; consistency delay vs collision-avoidance immediacy.
topics.counter_question: In your autonomous pipeline, do you run trajectory planning purely onboard or rely on an edge MEC server?

topics.title: Quantitative Infrastructure & Algorithmic Risk
questions: How do you ensure execution safety and sub-millisecond reliability in high-throughput trading systems?
How do you enforce strict risk limits like FTMO 5% daily drawdown automatically?
What is your approach to isolating market execution from risk governance?
topics.opening_hook: In algorithmic execution, latency without mathematical determinism is fatal—we strictly decouple the fast execution plane from a synchronous risk governor.
architecture_points: Dual-plane architecture: Order dispatchers talk directly over IPC/ZeroMQ to MT5 terminals while the Risk Governor enforces pre-trade invariants.
Hard-stop circuit breakers: Automated evaluations enforce a 5% max daily drawdown and 2% per-trade equity exposure before packets hit the wire.
Dynamic slippage bounds: Trades are rejected or routed through twap/vwap slices if market spread expands beyond 2.5 standard deviations.
Crash-resilient state journal: In-memory order state is continuously mirrored to append-only WAL backed by Redis on local memory.
metrics: < 2ms end-to-end order execution loop
Strict 100% FTMO drawdown compliance with zero breach history
Atomic execution kill-switch activated within 500 microseconds
topics.tradeoffs: Safety checks introduce microsecond jitter vs catastrophic capital liquidation risk.
topics.counter_question: Are your risk checks evaluated asynchronously via event stream or synchronously inline before order submission?

topics.title: High-Throughput Distributed Systems & Microservices
questions: How do you design a system that handles 100k requests per second with 99.99% availability?
How do you guarantee idempotency in distributed payment or messaging systems?
When would you choose event-driven choreography over orchestration?
topics.opening_hook: We design high-throughput systems around backpressure, bounded contexts, and explicit failure domains rather than unbounded horizontal scaling.
architecture_points: Asynchronous event ingestion: Edge traffic terminates at high-performance reverse proxies into Kafka/Pulsar partitioned queues with consumer group balancing.
Distributed idempotency keys: Requests carry unique client UUIDs validated in Redis using atomic SETNX with expiring TTLs before transactional processing.
Tiered cache architecture: L1 local in-process memory (Guava/Go cache) backed by L2 distributed Redis cluster with cache-aside and negative caching.
Database read/write segregation: CQRS pattern with write-optimized Postgres/Spanner and read-optimized replicated read pools.
metrics: Sub-15ms p99 read latency across multi-region deployment
Zero double-spend / duplicate execution via atomic Redis locks
100,000+ req/sec throughput with linear horizontal scaling
topics.tradeoffs: Eventual consistency lag vs distributed locking contention; complexity of distributed saga rollbacks.
topics.counter_question: What is your target p99 latency SLA, and are you optimizing primarily for read-heavy or write-heavy burst traffic?

topics.title: Cloud-Native Infrastructure, Kubernetes & GitOps
questions: How do you structure production Kubernetes clusters for zero-downtime deployments and resilience?
What is your philosophy on Infrastructure-as-Code and GitOps?
How do you handle observability and root-cause analysis in distributed microservices?
topics.opening_hook: Infrastructure must be completely declarative, immutable, and reproducible from Git commits down to bare metal.
architecture_points: Strict GitOps workflow: Cluster state is declared in Helm charts and Terraform, continuously reconciled via ArgoCD with automated canary rollouts.
Zero-trust pod security: Hardened distroless container images, non-root execution, mutual TLS (mTLS) via Istio, and automated network policies.
Unified telemetry pipeline: OpenTelemetry instrumentation feeding Prometheus metrics, Loki logs, and Tempo distributed tracing with unified trace-id correlation.
High-density resource governance: Explicit pod resource requests/limits, Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) driven by custom Prometheus metrics.
metrics: < 3 minute commit-to-production deployment cycle
Zero downtime rollouts with automated canary rollbacks on 5xx elevation
100% reproducible environments across dev, staging, and prod
topics.tradeoffs: Service mesh resource overhead vs observability/mTLS benefits; Canary complexity vs risk mitigation.
topics.counter_question: Are you currently using progressive delivery with automated canaries, or blue-green cutovers?

topics.title: CTO Leadership, Technical Debt & Incident Response
questions: Tell me about a major production outage you managed and how you handled it.
How do you balance aggressive feature delivery with paying down technical debt?
How do you foster high engineering standards across distributed teams?
topics.opening_hook: Elite engineering leadership is defined by psychological safety in post-mortems combined with zero tolerance for undisciplined architectural drift.
architecture_points: Incident Command System (ICS): Clear separation between the Incident Commander (who coordinates), technical responders, and the executive communications liaison.
Blameless Post-Mortems: Focus ruthlessly on systemic and tooling failure points rather than human error, generating actionable prevention tickets.
Technical Debt Budgeting: Allocate a continuous 20% engineering capacity to refactoring, tooling improvements, and dependency updates to prevent architectural debt accumulation.
Empowerment through Guardrails: Provide teams with robust CI/CD, automated linters, and architectural templates so they move fast with built-in safety.
metrics: Reduced MTTR (Mean Time To Recovery) from 45 min to < 8 min
99.99% multi-year service SLA across mission-critical systems
Zero recurring outages for previously documented failure modes
topics.tradeoffs: Immediate velocity vs architectural longevity; strict gating vs developer autonomy.
topics.counter_question: How is your engineering organization currently measuring and prioritizing technical debt alongside product roadmap commitments?

topics.title: Autonomous AI Agent Swarms & LLM Orchestration
questions: How do you build reliable, non-hallucinating AI agent systems in production?
What is your architecture for multi-agent collaboration and tool execution?
How do you handle context window management and memory in long-running agents?
topics.opening_hook: Production AI agents fail when treated like magic; they succeed when architected as deterministic state machines that leverage LLMs solely for classification and structured reasoning.
architecture_points: Structured Schema Enforcement: Agent outputs are strictly constrained by JSON schema validators (Pydantic / Instructor) with retry-on-violation loops.
Dual-tier memory mesh: Ephemeral working memory in Redis combined with long-term semantic indexing in vector stores using hybrid dense/sparse retrieval.
Model Context Protocol (MCP) tooling: Standardized interfaces for agent tools with deterministic sandboxing and permission boundaries.
Guardrail verifiers: Independent secondary evaluator agents that audit tool calls and outputs before critical mutations execute.
metrics: < 0.5% hallucination rate on structured domain extraction
Sub-second tool invocation routing via local semantic classifiers
100% auditable deterministic agent trace logs
topics.tradeoffs: Multiple evaluation passes increase token cost and latency vs output reliability.
topics.counter_question: What frameworks are you evaluating for agent orchestration, and how do you test agent behavior non-determinism in CI?
